allowedProcessNames.description: Case-insensitive process names the action's target must match.
allowedProcessNames.label: Allowed processes

allowedUrlPatterns.description: Regular expressions evaluated against the target browser tab's URL.
allowedUrlPatterns.label: Allowed URLs

allowedWindowTitlePatterns.description: Regular expressions evaluated against the target window's title.
allowedWindowTitlePatterns.label: Allowed window titles

automationPolicy.description: Extra constraints applied after permission gate + consent for Computer Use actions. Empty lists impose no constraint; any non-empty allowlist hard-fails actions whose facts don't satisfy it.
automationPolicy.emptyNote: No constraints configured — Computer Use actions follow only the permission gate and consent broker.

forbiddenScreenRegions.description: Pixel rectangles where clicks and drags are denied (password manager popups, system tray secrets, etc.).
forbiddenScreenRegions.label: Forbidden screen regions

automationPolicy.title: Per-action policy

canvasSandbox.description: Run code from the Canvas panel (Python especially) through the OS sandbox. When off, Canvas code runs unconfined with full host access.
canvasSandbox.label: Sandbox Canvas code execution
canvasSandbox.note: On by default. Disabling lets Canvas Python reach your filesystem and network — only turn it off on a machine you trust.
canvasSandbox.title: Canvas code sandbox

description: Per-platform OS sandbox for high-risk tools (Bash / Edit / Write / text_editor). When unavailable, strict mode refuses these tool calls instead of bypassing isolation.

enable.description: Run high-risk tools through the OS sandbox by default in every session. Individual sessions and characters can still override this.
enable.label: Enable sandbox by default
enable.note: Strict mode: when the sandbox backend is unavailable, sandboxed tool calls are refused rather than run unconfined.
enable.title: Default sandbox

allowlist.description: One host per line. Used when the ceiling is “Allowlist”. A leading *. matches subdomains.
allowlist.label: Allowed hosts

policy.description: The maximum resources and network reach a sandboxed shell may request. The model can ask for less, never more. Characters can override this default.

maxCpu.description: Upper bound on CPU-seconds per shell call. 0 = backend default.
maxCpu.label: Max CPU seconds

maxMemory.description: Upper bound on memory per shell call. 0 = backend default.
maxMemory.label: Max memory (MB)

network.description: The most a sandboxed shell may reach. “Off” forces every shell offline; “Allowlist” caps egress to the hosts below; “On” lets the model decide per call.
network.label: Network ceiling

policy.title: Resource & network ceiling

writableRoots.description: One absolute directory per line. When set, sandboxed writes are confined to these roots (and their subdirectories) — paths outside are dropped. Leave empty to allow any non-system location. System and app-data directories are always blocked.
writableRoots.errorForbidden: {path} cannot be used as a writable root. Choose a non-system directory inside a workspace or scratch area.
writableRoots.label: Writable roots (ceiling)

strictModeNote: Strict mode: when unavailable, sandboxed tool calls are refused — no bypass option.

tier.description: Which sandbox layer runs Bash / Edit / Write when a session has sandbox enabled. Characters can override.

microvm.description: Routes calls to an ephemeral Firecracker microVM via the cognia-e2b-sandbox plugin. Requires @e2b/sdk + E2B_API_KEY.
microvm.label: microVM (e2b Firecracker)

os.description: sandbox-exec on macOS, bwrap on Linux, codex-windows-sandbox on Windows. Lowest latency.
os.label: OS sandbox (default)

tier.title: Default sandbox tier

title: Sandbox

workspaceConfinement.description: Confine the built-in file and shell tools to the active workspace roots. Tools that try to write outside the workspace ask for approval first; credential paths (.ssh, .aws, …) are always blocked.
workspaceConfinement.label: Confine tools to the workspace
workspaceConfinement.note: On by default, and works on every platform. Disabling lets built-in tools read and write anywhere on this machine without asking. The OS sandbox, when enabled, supersedes this layer.
workspaceConfinement.title: Workspace confinement
